headline: High: shared file and network surfaces make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; TREK’s MCP/browser stack amplifies risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads and writes files and exposes stdin/stdout; Agent B uses MCP and browser-based workflows. If A’s outputs are placed into shared files or MCP-fed content, B can ingest attacker-controlled instructions. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A’s file outputs are consumed by B through MCP or browser-rendered content, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace without provenance tagging, B may treat A-authored content as instructions.
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct workspaces.
Disable MCP ingestion of untrusted files for B.
Add provenance labels to all A-generated artifacts.
Require manual review before B acts on A-produced text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles configuration secrets and can write files; B touches reservations, API keys, MFA secrets, and logs/uploads in a self-hosted collaborative app. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive data, and B’s browser/MCP surfaces increase the chance of onward transmission. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF A writes secrets or paper metadata into a shared directory, B can read them.
IF B uploads or logs A-produced files, sensitive content may be retained or exposed.
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Mount separate read/write directories for each agent.
Redact secrets before passing artifacts between agents.
Review B upload/log settings for sensitive content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files; B can use MCP and browser-based tools in a collaborative session. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared resources if co-located, creating race conditions or conflicting writes. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or database, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, one agent can overwrite the other’s artifacts.
mitigations: Assign disjoint writable paths.
Serialize write operations with a lock file.
Disable package installation in shared environments.
Use separate service accounts or containers.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research and content artifacts; B is a real-time collaborative planner that can consume external inputs through MCP and browser workflows. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can propagate into downstream travel actions or user-facing plans. No verification step is documented, so the cascade is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF B uses A outputs to draft plans or reservations, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source citations before B accepts A outputs.
Add a human approval step for any action derived from A.
Compare A outputs against primary sources before use.
Log provenance for every imported artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles academic papers, configuration secrets, and requested credentials; B handles reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. Both are open-source and docs-only, but B’s self-hosted collaborative travel stack and A’s local development environment create a plausible residency/retention mismatch for sensitive personal data. The profiles do not document compatible compliance controls.
conditions: IF EU personal data or travel records are processed by a non-EU-hosted deployment, residency risk arises.
IF either agent logs secrets or retains them beyond intended use, retention policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Confirm hosting region and retention settings.
Disable verbose logging for secrets.
Document deletion/export handling before use.
